name: Blood pressure (top number)
how_to_measure: Sit with your back supported and feet flat|Rest 5 minutes|Put the cuff on your bare upper arm at heart level|Take 2 readings 1 minute apart|Do not talk
how_to_measure_space: Stay still for 5 minutes in a foot or waist restraint|Keep the cuffed arm at heart level|Take 2 readings 1 minute apart|Do not talk
why_it_matters: High pressure makes your heart and blood vessels work harder.
what_to_do_yellow: Rest 5 minutes and measure again. One reading alone is not a reason to worry.
what_to_do_red: Measure again after 5 minutes of rest. If it is still red, Spica alerts your medical team. If you have chest pain, trouble breathing, weakness or trouble speaking, open the guide now.
source: S27; S28; S48 (space technique: demo); S61; S62
evidence_level: consensus (ranges, Earth technique); demo (space technique, SD)

name: Blood pressure (bottom number)
how_to_measure: Measured together with the top number
how_to_measure_space: Measured together with the top number
why_it_matters: The bottom number shows the pressure while your heart rests between beats.
what_to_do_yellow: Rest 5 minutes and measure again.
what_to_do_red: Measure again after 5 minutes of rest. If it is still red, Spica alerts your medical team.

name: Resting heart rate
how_to_measure: Rest 5 minutes|Count your pulse for 60 seconds, or read it on the oximeter
how_to_measure_space: Rest 5 minutes in a restraint|Count your pulse for 60 seconds, or read it on the oximeter
why_it_matters: A higher resting pulse can be a sign of poor sleep, illness or not enough water.
what_to_do_yellow: Rest, drink water and measure again in 5 minutes.
what_to_do_red: If you feel your heart racing, dizzy or faint, stop and open the guide. Spica alerts your medical team.

name: Oxygen (SpO₂)
frequency: daily, and when short of breath
how_to_measure: Warm your hand|Put the oximeter on a finger without nail polish|Keep still until the number is steady
why_it_matters: Shows how much oxygen your blood is carrying.
what_to_do_yellow: Warm your hand, keep still and measure again in 5 minutes. If you feel short of breath, trust how you feel even if the number looks normal.
what_to_do_red: Sit up, breathe slowly and open the guide. Spica alerts your medical team.
source: S32; S48 (oximeter accuracy note); S61; S62

name: Body temperature
frequency: daily, and before and after exercise or EVA
how_to_measure: Use the same thermometer in the same place every time|Wait 30 minutes after eating, drinking or exercise
how_to_measure_space: Use the forehead sensor|Same time of day, at rest
why_it_matters: A rise can mean infection or heat stress. In space your normal temperature slowly goes up about 1 °C, so Spica compares you with your own normal.
what_to_do_yellow: Rest, drink water and measure again in 15 minutes.
what_to_do_red: Stop exercise, cool down, drink water and open the guide. Spica alerts your medical team.
evidence_level: consensus (Earth fever cut-off); estimate (space rise); demo (space cut-offs)

name: Body mass
how_to_measure: Weigh yourself at the same time of day, after using the toilet, before eating
how_to_measure_space: Use the body-mass measuring device (inertial), same time of day
why_it_matters: Losing mass can mean you are not eating or drinking enough.
what_to_do_yellow: Check what you ate and drank this week.
what_to_do_red: Tell your medical team; Spica sends the trend.
evidence_level: demo (cut-offs, SD); NEEDS VALIDATION (ISS device name)

name: Sleep
how_to_measure: Write how many hours you slept, or use the sleep tracker
why_it_matters: Short sleep lowers attention and mood and makes mistakes more likely.
what_to_do_yellow: Keep your sleep time free, dim the lights before bed.
what_to_do_red: If you slept under 6 hours for 2 nights, avoid critical tasks and tell your medical team.
evidence_level: consensus (≥7 h); estimate (space ~6 h); demo (red rule)

name: Heart rhythm (ECG)
how_to_measure: Sit still|Place the electrodes or hold the ECG device|Stay still 30 seconds
how_to_measure_space: Stay still in a restraint 30 seconds
why_it_matters: Shows if your heartbeat is regular.
what_to_do_yellow: Rest and record again. Note any palpitations.
what_to_do_red: If your heart feels irregular with dizziness or chest pain, open the guide.

name: Breathing rate
frequency: daily, and when short of breath
how_to_measure: A crewmate counts how many times your chest rises in 30 seconds, twice, and doubles it|Breathe normally
why_it_matters: Fast breathing can be an early sign of a breathing or heart problem.
what_to_do_yellow: Rest and count again in 5 minutes.
what_to_do_red: Sit up, check oxygen and open the guide.

name: Blood sugar (fasting)
how_to_measure: Measure in the morning before eating|Use the glucose meter as trained
why_it_matters: Long missions may change how your body uses sugar.
what_to_do_yellow: If it is low (54–69), eat or drink fast sugar and measure again in 15 minutes. If it is high, measure again tomorrow.
what_to_do_red: If it is under 54, take fast sugar now and tell a crewmate. If it is high, Spica alerts your medical team.

name: Attention test (3 min)
frequency: weekly, and after a bad night
how_to_measure: Tap the screen as soon as the light appears|3 minutes
why_it_matters: Tiredness can slow you down without you noticing.
what_to_do_yellow: Rest or sleep before a critical task if you can. Check cabin CO₂.
what_to_do_red: Postpone critical tasks if possible and tell your medical team.

name: Radiation dose
how_to_measure: Wear your dosimeter at all times, also during spacewalks
why_it_matters: Radiation adds up over your career and raises long-term cancer risk.
what_to_do_yellow: Keep exposure as low as you can: limit time in less shielded areas.
what_to_do_red: Tell your medical team. Follow shelter instructions during a solar storm.

name: Hydration (urine colour)
how_to_measure: Compare your urine with the colour chart
why_it_matters: Not drinking enough raises the risk of kidney stones and makes you dizzy.
what_to_do_yellow: Drink a glass of water now and another within the hour.
what_to_do_red: Drink now, rest, and tell your medical team if you feel dizzy or confused.

name: Bone density
how_to_measure: Done by the medical team with a DXA scan
why_it_matters: Bones lose 1–1.5% of their mineral each month in space.
what_to_do_yellow: Keep up resistance exercise, calcium and vitamin D as advised.
what_to_do_red: Your medical team will plan your recovery.

name: Vision check
how_to_measure: Read the near and far charts, one eye at a time|Look at the Amsler grid with each eye
why_it_matters: Space can change the shape of the eye (SANS).
what_to_do_yellow: Measure again in a few days. Note blurred vision or wavy lines.
what_to_do_red: If you suddenly lose vision or see a dark area, open the guide now.

name: Aerobic fitness (VO₂max)
how_to_measure: Done by the medical team
how_to_measure_space: Not measured on board in this app
why_it_matters: Fitness drops without exercise in microgravity.
what_to_do_yellow: Keep up aerobic exercise.
what_to_do_red: Your medical team will plan your recovery.

name: Muscle strength
how_to_measure: Done by the medical team
how_to_measure_space: Not measured on board in this app
why_it_matters: Muscles shrink without load in microgravity.
what_to_do_yellow: Keep up resistance exercise.
what_to_do_red: Your medical team will plan your recovery.

name: Suit pressure
how_to_measure: Read from the suit
why_it_matters: If the suit loses pressure, you must act at once.
what_to_do_yellow: Check the suit display and tell the crew inside.
what_to_do_red: Follow your suit emergency procedure and head back to the airlock.
evidence_level: consensus (4.3 psi, ±0.25 stability); NEEDS VALIDATION (alarm limits)

name: Suit CO₂
how_to_measure: Read from the suit
why_it_matters: Too much CO₂ in the helmet causes headache and slows thinking.
what_to_do_yellow: Slow down and breathe steadily.
what_to_do_red: Open the purge valve as trained and tell the crew.

name: Time remaining
how_to_measure: Read from the suit
why_it_matters: Shows how long your oxygen and supplies last.
what_to_do_yellow: Plan your way back.
what_to_do_red: Head back to the airlock now.

name: Suit temperature
how_to_measure: Read from the suit
why_it_matters: Too hot or too cold in the suit affects your body and your work.
what_to_do_yellow: Adjust your cooling as trained.
what_to_do_red: Tell the crew and follow your suit procedure.

name: Cabin CO₂
how_to_measure: Read from the cabin sensor
why_it_matters: High CO₂ in the air can cause headache and tiredness.
what_to_do_yellow: Move to a better ventilated area and report it.
what_to_do_red: Report to the crew and Mission Control; open the guide if you have a headache.

name: Standing test (top number drop)
how_to_measure: Lie down 5 minutes and measure|Stand up with a helper beside you|Measure again at 1 and 3 minutes|If you feel dizzy, sit down and stop
why_it_matters: After space, blood pools in your legs when you stand, which can make you dizzy or fall.
what_to_do_yellow: Stand up slowly, drink water, have a helper nearby.
what_to_do_red: Sit or lie down now. Do not walk alone. Spica alerts your medical team.
source: S48 (consensus definition, citation NEEDS VALIDATION); S49

name: Standing test (bottom number drop)
how_to_measure: Measured together with the top number
why_it_matters: Same as the top number.
what_to_do_yellow: Same as the top number.
what_to_do_red: Same as the top number.
